newsitem.title: RWANDA: Fresh fighting erupts in Zairean border town.
newsitem.headline: Fresh fighting erupts in Zairean border town.

text.p: Fresh fighting erupted around the eastern Zairean border town of Uvira on Saturday between Zaire's armed forces and Banyamulenge Tutsi rebels, a spokesman for the U.N. refugee agency said.

"Renewed fighting has broken out this morning between the Banyamulenge and Zairean armed forces near Luvengi refugee camp," Paul Stromberg, spokesman for the U.N. High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) in Rwanda, told Reuters.
Stromberg gave no details, saying the refugee agency had failed to reach the fighting area.
He said Zairean residents had taken to the streets to demonstrate against the Banyamulenge.
On Friday, up to 26,400 mainly Burundi refugees fled their camp near Uvira after fighting between the Zairean military and ethnic Tutsi rebels left three dead, senior aid workers said.
The fighting was the second major round in Zaire in a week. Last Sunday about 20,000 Hutu refugees from Burundi fled their camp in eastern Zaire after it was attacked by armed men.

Fighting between Banyamulenge rebels and Zairean authorities trying to drive an estimated 200,000 Banyamulenge from a plateau west of Lake Tanganyika has left Zaire's South Kivu region in a virtual state of war.
Both Rwandan and Burundian refugees languish in camps north of Uvira, a town in the delta to the north west of Lake Tanganyika surrounded by steep hills.

Zaire accuses the Tutsi-dominated army of Rwanda, Burundi's northern neighbour, of training and arming the Banyamulenge guerrillas. Zaire's ragged army is fighting Banyamulenge guerrillas who are resisting the order to leave Zaire and return to Rwanda, a land they left as long as 200 years ago.
